headline: Bitcoin gave back its early gains and briefly dipped below $60,000 after US stocks opened, but it is still on course to end a seven-week losing streak, while US bitcoin funds are on track for their worst month on record.

market.asOf: Read from CoinMarketCap's cryptocurrency list at about 11:57 UTC Fri 27 Nov (18:57 Bangkok). Use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Alternative.me's index reads 11 out of 100 ("Extreme Fear", 13 a day earlier); CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index reads 10 ("Extreme fear"). Read about 11:57 UTC Fri 27 Nov.

stories.title: Bitcoin's Friday bounce fades below $60,000, but its losing streak could still end
stories.summary: Bitcoin rose to about $61,600 on Friday morning, on a day when about $7 billion of bitcoin options expired on Deribit, then briefly dipped below $60,000 shortly after US stocks opened, as Nvidia shares fell. A higher weekly close on Sunday would still end seven straight weekly losses.
points: Bitcoin had risen 1.8% since midnight UTC to around $61,600 by late morning UTC, per CoinDesk.
Early gains faded in the first 20 minutes of US trading and bitcoin slipped below $60,000 as Nvidia fell more than 2%, per CoinDesk's live blog at 9:50am ET (14:50 UTC).
A weekly gain would end seven straight weekly losses, the second-longest such streak on record; bitcoin is down about 20% in November, its worst month since June, per CoinDesk.
CoinDesk says a "death cross" (the 50-day average dropping below the 200-day average) is near, but notes the pattern usually appears after a decline has already started.
About $7 billion of bitcoin options expired on Deribit at 08:00 UTC, per CoinDesk.

sources.label: CoinDesk: bitcoin on course to end seven-week losing streak
CoinDesk Daybook: bitcoin death cross is coming

stories.title: US bitcoin funds head for a record-bad month, and Strategy leaves MSCI's indexes on Monday
stories.summary: November withdrawals from US spot bitcoin funds have already passed every previous month's total. MSCI's removal of Strategy (MSTR) from its indexes takes effect after Monday's close, which could prompt index funds to sell, while JPMorgan read Strategy's record-low value against its bitcoin as capitulation (sellers giving up).
points: US spot bitcoin funds lost $453.1 million on Wed 25 Nov, the seventh negative day in a row; BlackRock's IBIT led with $329.7 million, per The Block.
November outflows of $5.39 billion so far are already more than in any previous month, per The Block.
US spot ether funds lost $68.5 million on Wednesday, their ninth straight negative day, and $1.3 billion so far in November, per The Block.

Strategy's mNAV (market value divided by the value of its bitcoin) hit a record-low 0.88 on 25 Nov and later recovered to about 0.94; JPMorgan said the low signals capitulation in bitcoin, per Bitcoin.com News.

MSCI's removal of Strategy takes effect at the close on Mon 30 Nov; MSCI-linked funds hold about 13 million shares (about 3.1% of Strategy's shares), and JPMorgan estimated about $2.8 billion of selling, per Cointelegraph.

stories.title: Binance fully lifts its withdrawal freeze four weeks after the $6.3 billion hack
stories.summary: Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange, says withdrawals are back to normal after the 29 October hack. Withdrawals had been reopening in stages, and a few networks remain paused for maintenance.
points: Binance said "the withdrawal suspension from the October security incident has been fully lifted", per CoinDesk.
The hack affected about $6.3 billion in assets, of which about $3 billion was frozen, per CoinDesk.
Binance said it had restored 90% of the stolen crypto by 31 Oct, using company funds and its SAFU emergency reserve, and 98% of the $6.34 billion by 3 Nov, per CoinDesk.
Withdrawals for a small number of networks are still temporarily paused for maintenance or planned upgrades, per Binance via CoinDesk.
TRM Labs linked the attack to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, and the FBI also pointed to North Korea, per CoinDesk.

sources.label: CoinDesk: Binance says its withdrawal suspension is over

briefs.title: Monero has its worst day in over five months
briefs.summary: XMR fell more than 11% on Thursday, touching $430; KuCoin says it will delist XMR trading pairs at 08:00 UTC on 30 Nov, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Ripple's lending plan for the XRP Ledger is one vote short
briefs.summary: The vaults part of the plan has 29 of 35 validator votes and could switch on 9 Dec; the lending part has 28 votes, exactly 80%, one short of what it needs, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Injective asks the SEC to allow order books for tokenized stocks
briefs.summary: Injective asked the SEC to extend its proposed innovation exemption for tokenized US stocks to on-chain order-book venues, not just liquidity pools, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Ethereum sets a test date for its Glamsterdam upgrade
briefs.summary: Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade is cleared for a test on the Hoodi test network on 15 Dec, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: China, Japan, South Korea and ASEAN plan a crypto working group
briefs.summary: The countries will form a working group on digital payments and crypto regulation, per The Block.

calendar.event: US stock markets close early after Thanksgiving
calendar.note: Stocks close at 1:00pm ET, per NYSE; SIFMA recommends a 2:00pm ET early close for US bond markets.

calendar.event: Binance Blockchain Week, Bangkok; Fed quiet period begins
calendar.note: At the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center, per Khaosod English. The Fed's pre-meeting blackout runs from Sat 28 Nov to Thu 10 Dec, per Admiral Markets.

calendar.note: PROS and GRASS on Saturday 28; FF and CARDS on Sunday 29; GRVT, KMNO and GUN on Monday 30 (one tracker gives GUN on the 29th); EIGEN and SUI on Tuesday 1 Dec; M, BTW, ENA, 2Z and Q on Wednesday 2 Dec (M's date is disputed: Tokenomist shows 12 Dec); STO on Thursday 3 Dec; MMT and LA on Friday 4 Dec. calendar.event: Trump Media (DJT) noteholders can demand repayment
calendar.note: Holders of its convertible notes can require the company to buy them back for cash; about $883.5 million is outstanding after a $100 million buyback, and its filing warns it may need to sell bitcoin to fund repurchases, per CoinDesk.

calendar.event: MSCI removes Strategy (MSTR) from its indexes
calendar.note: Takes effect at the close on 30 Nov. MSCI-linked funds hold about 13 million MSTR shares, about 3.1% of its shares outstanding; JPMorgan estimated about $2.8 billion of selling, per Cointelegraph.

calendar.event: ISM manufacturing PMI (Nov), job openings (JOLTS, Oct); Fed's Bowman testifies to the House
calendar.note: ISM: October was 55.5, per ISM; Wells Fargo expects 53.8, per ActionForex. JOLTS: September was about 7.5 million, per the BLS; the BLS schedules October's release for 10:00am. Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman testifies at the House Financial Services "Oversight of Prudential Regulators" hearing, per the Fed's calendar. Marvell reports the same day, with its call at 4:30pm ET, per its investor page.

calendar.event: ADP private payrolls (Nov); Salesforce and Snowflake earnings
calendar.note: ADP's release is at 8:15am ET, per FinanceCalendar; October was +86,000, per Fox Business. Salesforce and Snowflake report after the close, per their investor pages.

calendar.event: US jobless claims; ISM services PMI (Nov); Nvidia's Huang before the Senate
calendar.note: Claims fell to 189,000 in the week to 21 Nov, per the Labor Department. ISM services: October was 54.5, per investingLive; Wells Fargo expects 54.9, per ActionForex. The Senate Banking Committee chairman set a public hearing with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang for 10:00am ET on 3 Dec, per Yahoo News.

A Reuters poll expects +90,000 jobs, per Reuters' Take Five; ING and Wells Fargo expect +80,000 with unemployment at 4.1%. October payrolls rose 165,000 and unemployment was 4.1%, per Fox Business. Release at 8:30am ET, per the BLS.

Markets expect a rate hike, not a cut: CME FedWatch showed a 97.4% chance of a quarter-point hike late on 26 Nov, per Longbridge, and Reuters says the debate is between a quarter-point and a half-point move. The Fed's calendar lists the decision at 2:00pm ET and the press conference at 2:30pm ET.
